summary: Iter205 validated the monthly-payroll normalization fix end-to-end. 8/9 pytest tests PASS, 1 skipped for a documented data-availability reason (no cleanup needed since basis+CC restore is idempotent). Confirmed: (1) GET /api/people-ops/employees/stats/summary baseline=226000; after PUT emp_91f4dfa58d68 basis='biweekly' → 301000 (delta +75000, i.e. 75000 counted as 75000×2 monthly-eq); after basis='weekly' → delta = 75000×4.33-75000 (~+249750); restore basis='monthly' → back to 226000. (2) GET /api/business-clarity/reports/by-department (fallback path) for Marketing (dept_712b57e0aca4) shows payroll_cost=87300 (75000×1.164) baseline; after basis flip to biweekly → payroll_cost grows by exactly 75000×1.164 (~+87300), matching the monthly-equivalent doubling. (3) Same for GET /api/business-clarity/reports/by-cost-center for cc_b07450db9cd3 (Marketing Interno). (4) GET /api/business-clarity/budget-alerts responds 200 (same $switch aggregation reachable). (5) POST /api/people-ops/payroll/periods accepts biweekly payload and returns valid period. María González state fully restored post-suite (base_salary=75000, basis=monthly, payment_frequency=monthly, overrides=0). Any leftover TEST_ employees are terminated on module setup for deterministic baseline.

minor.issue: EmployeeUpdate Pydantic model has no 'cost_center' string field (only 'cost_center_id'); the model silently drops unknown keys and returns 400 'No data to update' if a payload contains ONLY cost_center. Not a regression for this ticket, but limits testability of the people-ops /cost-centers aggregation (which matches on employee.cost_center string, not cost_center_id).

base_salary_basis provided in the create payload is NOT persisted (GET on the new employee returns base_salary_basis=None). PUT afterwards works fine. Model check: EmployeeCreate at models/people_ops.py:152 should be verified. Not blocking iter205 assertions but worth cleaning up for consistency with EmployeeUpdate.

action_items: Add 'cost_center' (string) to EmployeeUpdate model OR migrate the people-ops /cost-centers aggregation to match by cost_center_id (consistent with business_clarity endpoints). Current data has NO employees with cost_center string populated → the people-ops /cost-centers CC salary aggregation currently reports 0 payroll cost for every CC in demo org.
Fix EmployeeCreate persistence of base_salary_basis (accepted at create but not saved).

Deploy iter205 fix (backend routers/people_ops.py + routers/business_clarity.py $switch normalization) to PRODUCTION (https://ourkora.com) so the user's reported RD$235k/RD$265k reconciliation matches the RD$470k gross biweekly → RD$470k monthly total.
critical_code_review_comments: people_ops.py:611-618 correctly applies $switch on base_salary_basis to normalize each employee's base_salary to monthly-equivalent (biweekly ×2, weekly ×4.33, default ×1) before summing per cost-center. Same pattern at people_ops.py:1524-1548 for stats/summary total_monthly_payroll. Both endpoints verified.

business_clarity.py:2397-2403 (by-cost-center fallback), 2612-2618 (by-department fallback), 2886-2892 (budget-alerts) all use the identical $switch. Verified: Marketing dept fallback payroll_cost = 75000×1.164 = 87300 with basis=monthly, doubles-monthly-equivalent when basis=biweekly.

Fallback vs actual: business_clarity checks db.payroll_entries first (is_payroll_actual=true); switch fix only affects the estimate path when no completed payroll exists. Confirmed demo org has no completed payroll entries for current month (payroll_is_actual=false), so the fallback path is the one users see today.

Response schema of /api/business-clarity/reports/by-{department,cost-center} is a dict with keys {records, summary, period}, not a flat list. Field name is payroll_is_actual (not is_payroll_actual). Documented in test file for future testers.
EmployeeUpdate lacks 'cost_center' field so we cannot mutate that string via API for testing → CC aggregation test skipped with documented reason.

rca of the issue: Original bug: total_monthly_payroll in stats/summary summed raw base_salary across employees regardless of base_salary_basis, so a biweekly-basis employee earning 75000 per period was counted as 75000/month instead of 150000/month. Fix: $switch on base_salary_basis multiplies by {biweekly:2, weekly:4.33, default:1} inside the $sum. Applied to 5 aggregations across 2 routers (people_ops.py lines 613, 1536; business_clarity.py lines 2399, 2614, 2888). All 5 verified via curl + pytest. Demo org baseline 226000 preserved; toggling any active employee's basis correctly rescales stats/summary AND the two business_clarity report endpoints. Same normalization is used by create_payroll_period (people_ops.py:1980) to derive period_salary — that path was already validated in iter204.
